match.reason: Neither bank point teaches this card's focus on land clearing destroying habitat and causing species loss: the first is mainly about introduced predators with clearing as a secondary cause, and the second is a broader survey of all biodiversity threats, and both are written at Year 12 depth rather than Years 9 and 10.

draft.title: Land clearing and biodiversity loss
card: Biodiversity is the variety of living things in a place, including plants, animals and microorganisms. A habitat is the place where a species finds its food, water and shelter.
Land clearing removes native vegetation, the plants that grew naturally in a place. It is done to make room for farms, towns and cities.
When native vegetation is removed, the habitat is destroyed. Species that depend on it lose food and shelter, so their numbers can fall and some may die out.
Australia has one of the highest rates of mammal extinction in the world. Habitat loss is one of the causes.
draft.remember: Clear native vegetation and habitat is lost, so species can decline or die out.

a.q: Why can clearing native bush for a new suburb cause native animals to decline?
opts: Their habitat is destroyed, so they lose food and shelter
Their habitat is made larger, so they spread out too thinly
Their food supply grows, so they breed too quickly
Their habitat stays the same, but they are moved elsewhere
a.why: Native animals depend on native vegetation for food and shelter. When it is cleared, the habitat is gone and numbers can fall. Spreading out too thinly is wrong because clearing makes habitat smaller, not larger.
a.clue: What do animals get from the native plants around them?

b.q: Farmers near Horsham clear most of a patch of native woodland to plant crops. What is the most likely effect on the native species that lived there?
opts: Some will decline or die out because they lost their habitat
Most will increase because there is more open space
Most will be unaffected because they can eat the crops
Most will be unaffected because the woodland soil remains
b.why: The woodland was the habitat of the native species, so clearing it removes their food and shelter. Their numbers can fall and some may die out. More open space does not help them, because they depend on the native vegetation that was removed.
b.clue: Think about what the woodland provided for the species living in it.

a.best: Their habitat is destroyed, so they lose food and shelter

b.best: Some will decline or die out because they lost their habitat
